result.summary: The street features narrow sidewalks directly adjacent to the roadway with no buffer from traffic. While stop signs control the upcoming intersection, there are no marked crosswalks or traffic calming measures visible to protect pedestrians.

hazards.name: Unmarked Intersection
hazards.description: The intersection ahead lacks marked crosswalks, making pedestrian movements less predictable for drivers.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked cars close to the intersection may block the view between pedestrians waiting to cross and approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Right and left sides of the street near the intersection.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental or ladder-style marked crosswalks at all legs of the intersection.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Add curb extensions (bulb-outs) to shorten crossing distances and improve pedestrian visibility.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the intersection to improve sightlines.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a narrow, poorly maintained sidewalk with significant cracking and debris. There is no physical buffer between the walkway and the roadway, and the lack of street trees or traffic calming measures contributes to a low-quality walking experience.

hazards.name: Degraded Sidewalk Surface
hazards.description: The sidewalk is heavily cracked and uneven, creating significant trip hazards for pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image, along the building frontages.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: Trash bags and utility poles narrow the effective walking width of the already narrow sidewalk.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground left and middle ground right on the sidewalk.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Reconstruction
interventions.description: Repair and level the sidewalk to ensure a continuous, ADA-compliant walking surface.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Greenery
interventions.description: Install street trees or planters to provide a physical and psychological buffer between pedestrians and the roadway.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Add lighting specifically for the sidewalk to improve visibility and safety at night.

result.summary: A narrow residential street lined with row houses and parallel parking on both sides. The pedestrian environment is constrained by narrow sidewalks that are further obstructed by utility poles and lack any marked crossing infrastructure.

hazards.name: Utility pole obstructions
hazards.description: Utility poles are located directly in the center of the narrow sidewalk, significantly reducing the effective width for pedestrians, especially those with mobility aids or strollers.
hazards.location_in_image: Left and right sidewalks along the block

hazards.name: Sightline obstructions
hazards.description: Continuous parallel parking on both sides of the street creates visual barriers between drivers and pedestrians attempting to cross.

hazards.name: Lack of marked crossings
hazards.description: There are no marked crosswalks or pedestrian warning signs visible, providing no designated safe space for crossing the street.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at intersections to shorten crossing distances and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Add marked crosswalks with high-visibility paint to designate pedestrian priority areas.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Buffer Zone
interventions.description: Introduce street trees or a furniture zone to create a physical buffer between the narrow sidewalk and moving traffic.

result.summary: The image depicts a narrow residential street with a continuous concrete sidewalk that lacks a buffer from the roadway. The environment is characterized by row-house architecture with minimal greenery and some visible litter on the ground.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: The sidewalk is directly adjacent to the travel lane without any physical separation like a planting strip or furniture zone.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the entire length of the sidewalk edge

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Vehicle
hazards.description: A parked vehicle on the left side of the frame partially blocks sightlines between the sidewalk and the roadway.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Planters
interventions.description: Introduce street trees or large planters to create a physical and psychological buffer between the walkway and moving traffic.

interventions.description: Install street lighting designed for pedestrians to improve visibility and perceived safety during evening hours.
